fullPassage: There is a natural assumption of truth, or a truth bias when humans communicate with one another. In other words, when we're listening to others or reading their words, our automatic assumption is that the other person is telling the truth. This usually works out fine. If you ask someone where the restroom is located or if it's raining outside, you can safely assume that most people will not lie in their responses. Imagine how difficult it would be to converse with someone if you assumed that everything they were telling you was false! Indeed, questioning the truth of a statement and then choosing not to believe it requires additional mental steps. For the most part, humans are "cognitive misers," which means we typically don't expend more mental effort than seems necessary in a given situation. It makes sense then, that when we see something online, even if it is fake, our default is to believe it, at least at first.

det.korean: cognitive misers: 인지적 구두쇠 (필요 이상의 정신적 노력을 하지 않는 사람들)
det.analysis:
① cognitive misers(인지적 구두쇠) ← 정답: '필요 이상의 정신적 노력을 소비하지 않는다'는 뒤 설명과 정확히 일치
② mental steps(정신적 단계): 인간의 특성이 아닌 과정을 나타내는 표현 — 빈칸 뒤 which means 이하와 연결 안 됨 ❌
③ truth bias(진실 편향): 글 앞부분에서 이미 설명된 개념 — 빈칸은 인간의 다른 특성을 설명 ❌
④ automatic assumption(자동적 가정): 앞 문장에서 이미 언급된 개념 — 새로운 설명이 아님 ❌
det.tip: cognitive misers = 인지적 구두쇠 (정신적 에너지 절약)

questions.passage: There is a natural assumption of truth, or a truth bias when humans communicate with one another. In other words, when we're listening to others or reading their words, our automatic assumption is that the other person is telling the truth. This usually works out fine. If you ask someone where the restroom is located or if it's raining outside, you can safely assume that most people will not lie in their responses. Imagine how difficult it would be to converse with someone if you assumed that everything they were telling you was false! Indeed, questioning the truth of a statement and then choosing not to believe it requires additional mental steps. For the most part, humans are "cognitive misers," which means we typically don't expend more mental effort than seems necessary in a given situation. It makes sense then, that when we see something online, even if it is fake, our default is to believe it, __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: our default is to believe it, _____ → at least at first(최소한 처음에는).
det.analysis:
① in a given situation: 특정 상황에서 — 문맥 부적합 ❌
② in their responses: 응답에서 — 문맥 부적합 ❌
③ at least at first: 최소한 처음에는 ← 정답
④ in other words: 다시 말해 — 문맥 부적합 ❌
